sources.title: Council of Europe: CEFR Companion Volume (2020)

units.title: Tell a connected story
units.description: Place background, completed events and earlier actions on one timeline.

lessons.title: Background meets event
lessons.outcome: I can set a scene and name the event that interrupted it.
lessons.takeaway: Use the passato prossimo for the bounded event that happens during that background.

objectives.label: Background meets event
objectives.explanation: Use the imperfetto for a situation or action in progress in the past. Use the passato prossimo for the bounded event that happens during that background.

teach.title: Ongoing background
teach.body: Use the imperfetto for a situation or action in progress in the past.

examples.it: Leggevo sul divano.
examples.en: I was reading on the sofa.

teach.title: Completed event
teach.body: Use the passato prossimo for the bounded event that happens during that background.

examples.it: Leggevo quando è suonato il telefono.
examples.en: I was reading when the phone rang.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Mentre ___, è arrivato Luca.
questions.translation: While I was cooking, Luca arrived.
questions.explanation: The cooking was already in progress when Luca arrived.
questions.hint: Think of the activity in progress.
questions.speak: Mentre cucinavo, è arrivato Luca.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Pioveva quando noi ___ a casa.
questions.translation: It was raining when we got home.
questions.explanation: The arrival is the completed event against the rainy background.
questions.hint: Use the passato prossimo of arrivare with essere.
questions.speak: Pioveva quando noi siamo arrivati a casa.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Giulia ___ quando è caduta la luce.
questions.translation: Giulia was studying when the power went out.
questions.explanation: Studying was the background action.
questions.hint: Which tense describes an ongoing scene?
questions.speak: Giulia studiava quando è caduta la luce.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I was sleeping when you knocked.
questions.explanation: Dormivo sets the background; hai bussato marks the interruption.
questions.hint: Put the ongoing action first.
questions.speak: Dormivo quando hai bussato.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.left: Leggevo quando è suonato il telefono.
pairs.right: a background action interrupted by one event
one completed reading yesterday
a repeated childhood habit

questions.explanation: Imperfetto sets a scene or routine; passato prossimo bounds a completed event.
questions.hint: Look at quando, ieri and ogni sera.
questions.speak: Leggevo quando è suonato il telefono.

lessons.title: Before another past event
lessons.outcome: I can show that one past action happened before another.
lessons.takeaway: The later event commonly uses passato prossimo or imperfetto; the earlier one uses trapassato prossimo.

objectives.label: Before another past event
objectives.explanation: Imperfetto of avere or essere plus a past participle places an event earlier than a past reference point. The later event commonly uses passato prossimo or imperfetto; the earlier one uses trapassato prossimo.

teach.title: Build the trapassato
teach.body: Imperfetto of avere or essere plus a past participle places an event earlier than a past reference point.

examples.it: Quando sono arrivato, Anna era già partita.
examples.en: When I arrived, Anna had already left.

teach.title: Keep the timeline clear
teach.body: The later event commonly uses passato prossimo or imperfetto; the earlier one uses trapassato prossimo.

examples.it: Non avevo fame perché avevo già mangiato.
examples.en: I was not hungry because I had already eaten.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Quando siamo entrati, il film ___ già iniziato.
questions.translation: When we entered, the film had already started.
questions.explanation: The film started before we entered; era iniziato is trapassato.
questions.hint: Choose the imperfect auxiliary.
questions.speak: Quando siamo entrati, il film era già iniziato.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Ho aperto la borsa, ma ___ il portafoglio a casa.
questions.translation: I opened my bag, but I had left my wallet at home.
questions.explanation: The leaving happened earlier than opening the bag.
questions.hint: Use avevo plus the participle.
questions.speak: Ho aperto la borsa, ma avevo lasciato il portafoglio a casa.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Giulia era stanca perché ___ dormito poco.
questions.translation: Giulia was tired because she had slept little.
questions.explanation: The lack of sleep came before her tiredness.
questions.hint: Use the imperfect of avere.
questions.speak: Giulia era stanca perché aveva dormito poco.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: We had booked before leaving.
questions.explanation: Avevamo prenotato locates the booking before the departure.
questions.hint: Use avevamo with the participle.
questions.speak: Avevamo prenotato prima di partire.

lessons.title: Repeated life in the past
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish an old routine from a single completed occasion.
lessons.takeaway: A dated or singled-out event normally takes passato prossimo in conversational narration.

objectives.label: Repeated life in the past
objectives.explanation: Use imperfetto with habitual markers such as ogni estate or da bambino. A dated or singled-out event normally takes passato prossimo in conversational narration.

teach.title: Routine in the background
teach.body: Use imperfetto with habitual markers such as ogni estate or da bambino.

examples.it: Da piccola andavo spesso al mare.
examples.en: As a child, I often went to the sea.

teach.title: A particular occasion
teach.body: A dated or singled-out event normally takes passato prossimo in conversational narration.

examples.it: L’estate scorsa sono andata a Bari.
examples.en: Last summer I went to Bari.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Da bambino ___ ogni domenica dai nonni.
questions.translation: As a child I used to go to my grandparents every Sunday.
questions.explanation: Ogni domenica marks a past habit.
questions.hint: Use imperfetto for a repeated past routine.
questions.speak: Da bambino andavo ogni domenica dai nonni.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Ieri, invece, ___ dai nonni solo per un’ora.
questions.translation: Yesterday, instead, I stayed only for an hour.
questions.explanation: Ieri and a bounded duration identify one completed visit.
questions.hint: Use a completed past tense with essere.
questions.speak: Ieri, invece, sono rimasto dai nonni solo per un’ora.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Un tempo qui ___ un cinema.
questions.translation: There used to be a cinema here.
questions.explanation: Un tempo describes a past state over a stretch of time.
questions.hint: Use the imperfect of esserci.
questions.speak: Un tempo qui c’era un cinema.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: Every Friday we used to have dinner together.
questions.explanation: Ogni venerdì establishes a repeated past action.
questions.hint: Choose imperfetto for the old routine.
questions.speak: Ogni venerdì cenavamo insieme.

units.title: Refer back without repeating
units.description: Combine small pronouns and replace places or quantities clearly.

lessons.title: Give it to someone
lessons.outcome: I can combine an indirect object pronoun with a direct one.
lessons.takeaway: Gli and le both form glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele; context tells the recipient.

objectives.label: Give it to someone
objectives.explanation: The indirect pronoun comes first: mi, ti, gli/le becomes me, te, glie- before lo, la, li, le. Gli and le both form glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele; context tells the recipient.

teach.title: Order of two pronouns
teach.body: The indirect pronoun comes first: mi, ti, gli/le becomes me, te, glie- before lo, la, li, le.

examples.it: Il libro? Te lo presto domani.
examples.en: The book? I’ll lend it to you tomorrow.

teach.title: One written word for glie-
teach.body: Gli and le both form glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele; context tells the recipient.

examples.it: La foto? Gliela mando stasera.
examples.en: The photo? I’ll send it to him or her tonight.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Hai il numero? Sì, ___ mando subito.
questions.translation: Do you have the number? Yes, I’ll send it to you right away.
questions.explanation: Te lo combines to you + it (the masculine numero).
questions.hint: Ti changes to te before lo.
questions.speak: Hai il numero? Sì, te lo mando subito.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: La chiave è di Marta. Domani ___ restituisco.
questions.translation: The key belongs to Marta. Tomorrow I’ll give it back to her.
questions.explanation: Gliela combines to her + the feminine chiave.
questions.hint: To her + la becomes one word.
questions.speak: La chiave è di Marta. Domani gliela restituisco.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Questi documenti sono per me? Sì, ___ porto domani.
questions.translation: Are these documents for me? Yes, I’ll bring them to you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Te li means to you + them (masculine plural).
questions.hint: Put the recipient before the object.
questions.speak: Questi documenti sono per me? Sì, te li porto domani.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: Can you explain it to me?
questions.explanation: Me precedes lo in a two-pronoun group.
questions.hint: Order recipient then object.
questions.speak: Me lo puoi spiegare?

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: I send it to you.
I bring it to him or her.
They give them to us.

questions.explanation: The first pronoun marks the recipient, the second the object.
questions.hint: Identify who receives each object.
questions.speak: Te lo mando.

lessons.title: Ci for a place
lessons.outcome: I can refer back to a known place with ci.
lessons.takeaway: With a finite verb, ci normally goes immediately before it.

objectives.label: Ci for a place
objectives.explanation: Ci can stand for a place already mentioned, often with andare, essere or tornare. With a finite verb, ci normally goes immediately before it.

teach.title: Replace a place
teach.body: Ci can stand for a place already mentioned, often with andare, essere or tornare.

examples.it: Vai spesso a Roma? Sì, ci vado ogni mese.
examples.en: Do you go to Rome often? Yes, I go there every month.

teach.title: Position before the verb
teach.body: With a finite verb, ci normally goes immediately before it.

examples.it: In biblioteca ci studio meglio.
examples.en: I study better in the library.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Conosci quel bar? Sì, ___ vado spesso.
questions.translation: Do you know that café? Yes, I often go there.
questions.explanation: Ci refers back to the café as a destination.
questions.hint: Think “there” with andare.
questions.speak: Conosci quel bar? Sì, ci vado spesso.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Sei mai stata a Napoli? Sì, ___ sono stata due volte.
questions.translation: Have you ever been to Naples? Yes, I have been there twice.
questions.explanation: Ci replaces a Napoli.
questions.hint: Use the place pronoun before sono.
questions.speak: Sei mai stata a Napoli? Sì, ci sono stata due volte.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Torni in ufficio dopo pranzo? Sì, ___ torno alle due.
questions.translation: Are you returning to the office after lunch? Yes, I return there at two.
questions.explanation: Ci refers to the office, the destination.
questions.hint: Use the pronoun for a known place.
questions.speak: Torni in ufficio dopo pranzo? Sì, ci torno alle due.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: We are going there tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: Ci appears before the finite verb and refers to the known destination.
questions.hint: Start with the place pronoun.
questions.speak: Ci andiamo domani mattina.

lessons.title: Ne for some or of it
lessons.outcome: I can replace a previously named quantity or di phrase with ne.
lessons.takeaway: Ne can replace di questo, di lui, di loro after verbs such as parlare.

objectives.label: Ne for some or of it
objectives.explanation: Ne means some of them or of it; keep the quantity word if it matters. Ne can replace di questo, di lui, di loro after verbs such as parlare.

teach.title: Part of a set
teach.body: Ne means some of them or of it; keep the quantity word if it matters.

examples.it: Quante mele vuoi? Ne prendo tre.
examples.en: How many apples do you want? I’ll take three.

teach.title: A di topic
teach.body: Ne can replace di questo, di lui, di loro after verbs such as parlare.

examples.it: Parliamo del viaggio? Ne parliamo dopo.
examples.en: Shall we talk about the trip? We’ll talk about it later.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Hai comprato delle arance? Sì, ___ ho prese quattro.
questions.translation: Did you buy oranges? Yes, I bought four of them.
questions.explanation: Ne stands for some oranges; quattro states the number.
questions.hint: Think “of them” before ho.
questions.speak: Hai comprato delle arance? Sì, ne ho prese quattro.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Quanti biglietti vi servono? ___ servono due.
questions.translation: How many tickets do you need? We need two of them.
questions.explanation: Ce ne preserves the of-them meaning and the recipient “us.”
questions.hint: Use the two-pronoun form before servono.
questions.speak: Quanti biglietti vi servono? Ce ne servono due.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Parlate ancora di quel problema? Sì, ___ parliamo spesso.
questions.translation: Do you still talk about that problem? Yes, we often talk about it.
questions.explanation: Parlare di takes ne for the di phrase.
questions.hint: Which pronoun replaces di quel problema?
questions.speak: Parlate ancora di quel problema? Sì, ne parliamo spesso.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: We bought three of them.
questions.explanation: Ne refers to an understood masculine plural item; tre specifies quantity.
questions.hint: Put ne before abbiamo.
questions.speak: Ne abbiamo comprati tre.

units.title: Join descriptions
units.description: Make smooth relative clauses with subject, object and prepositional links.

lessons.title: Che and cui
lessons.outcome: I can link a noun to a clause using che or cui.
lessons.takeaway: Use cui for an indirect relationship such as a cui or di cui.

objectives.label: Che and cui
objectives.explanation: Che links a noun to a clause when the noun is subject or direct object there. Use cui for an indirect relationship such as a cui or di cui.

teach.title: Che for subject or object
teach.body: Che links a noun to a clause when the noun is subject or direct object there.

examples.it: La persona che parla è mia sorella.
examples.en: The person who is speaking is my sister.

teach.title: Cui after a preposition
teach.body: Use cui for an indirect relationship such as a cui or di cui.

examples.it: È il collega di cui ti parlavo.
examples.en: He is the colleague I was telling you about.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Il libro ___ leggo è di Elena.
questions.translation: The book that I am reading is Elena’s.
questions.explanation: The book is the direct object of leggo, so use che.
questions.hint: No preposition is needed before the object.
questions.speak: Il libro che leggo è di Elena.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Questa è l’amica ___ ti ho parlato.
questions.translation: This is the friend I told you about.
questions.explanation: Parlare di requires di cui in the relative clause.
questions.hint: Remember parlare di qualcuno.
questions.speak: Questa è l’amica di cui ti ho parlato.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: La donna ___ ci ha aiutato lavora qui.
questions.translation: The woman who helped us works here.
questions.explanation: The woman is the subject of ha aiutato; che links it.
questions.hint: Use the simple subject relative.
questions.speak: La donna che ci ha aiutato lavora qui.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I know the boy who works here.
questions.answer: Conosco il ragazzo che lavora qui.
questions.explanation: Che joins ragazzo to the clause where he is the subject.
questions.hint: Place che after the noun it describes.
questions.speak: Conosco il ragazzo che lavora qui.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.left: La ragazza che canta è mia sorella.
pairs.right: The girl who sings is my sister.

pairs.left: Il collega di cui parlo è qui.
pairs.right: The colleague I talk about is here.

pairs.left: La persona a cui scrivo abita a Roma.
pairs.right: The person I write to lives in Rome.

questions.explanation: Che links a subject; preposition plus cui preserves the verb relation.
questions.hint: Think of parlare di and scrivere a.
questions.speak: La ragazza che canta è mia sorella.

lessons.title: The right preposition before cui
lessons.outcome: I can carry a verb’s required preposition into a relative clause.
lessons.takeaway: Use in cui for “in which/when” and a cui for “to whom/which.”

objectives.label: The right preposition before cui
objectives.explanation: If you say parlare con Marco, say Marco con cui parlo. Use in cui for “in which/when” and a cui for “to whom/which.”

teach.title: Keep the governed preposition
teach.body: If you say parlare con Marco, say Marco con cui parlo.

examples.it: La donna con cui lavoro è gentile.
examples.en: The woman I work with is kind.

teach.title: Time and place links
teach.body: Use in cui for “in which/when” and a cui for “to whom/which.”

examples.it: Ricordo il giorno in cui ci siamo conosciuti.
examples.en: I remember the day when we met.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Ecco la collega ___ ho scritto ieri.
questions.translation: Here is the colleague I wrote to yesterday.
questions.explanation: Scrivere a qualcuno becomes a cui in a relative clause.
questions.hint: Keep the a from scrivere a.
questions.speak: Ecco la collega a cui ho scritto ieri.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Questa è la stanza ___ si tiene la riunione.
questions.translation: This is the room in which the meeting takes place.
questions.explanation: The meeting takes place in the room, so use in cui.
questions.hint: Which preposition marks location inside?
questions.speak: Questa è la stanza in cui si tiene la riunione.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Il progetto ___ lavoriamo è quasi finito.
questions.translation: The project we are working on is almost finished.
questions.explanation: Lavorare a un progetto requires a cui.
questions.hint: Keep the a from lavorare a.
questions.speak: Il progetto a cui lavoriamo è quasi finito.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: It is the city in which I was born.
questions.answer: È la città in cui sono nato.
questions.explanation: In cui links the city to the location of birth.
questions.hint: Use in before cui for the location.
questions.speak: È la città in cui sono nato.

units.title: Express a viewpoint
units.description: Use the present subjunctive after opinion, wishes and impersonal evaluation.

lessons.title: I think, I doubt
lessons.outcome: I can use the present subjunctive after uncertain opinions.
lessons.takeaway: Dubito che and non sono sicuro che also invite the subjunctive.

objectives.label: I think, I doubt
objectives.explanation: Penso che and credo che commonly introduce a present subjunctive when making a personal judgment. Dubito che and non sono sicuro che also invite the subjunctive.

teach.title: Opinion plus che
teach.body: Penso che and credo che commonly introduce a present subjunctive when making a personal judgment.

examples.it: Penso che Maria sia a casa.
examples.en: I think Maria is at home.

teach.title: Doubt or uncertainty
teach.body: Dubito che and non sono sicuro che also invite the subjunctive.

examples.it: Dubito che il negozio sia aperto.
examples.en: I doubt the shop is open.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Penso che Luca ___ ragione.
questions.translation: I think Luca is right.
questions.explanation: A personal opinion introduced by penso che takes abbia.
questions.hint: Use the present subjunctive of avere.
questions.speak: Penso che Luca abbia ragione.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Dubito che loro ___ la risposta.
questions.translation: I doubt they know the answer.
questions.explanation: Doubt calls for the present subjunctive sappiano.
questions.hint: Use the loro form of sapere in the subjunctive.
questions.speak: Dubito che loro sappiano la risposta.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Credo che Giulia ___ domani.
questions.translation: I think Giulia is coming tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Credo che expresses a viewpoint, so venga fits.
questions.hint: Use the present subjunctive of venire.
questions.speak: Credo che Giulia venga domani.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I think you are right.
questions.explanation: Penso che introduces a personal opinion; abbia is subjunctive.
questions.hint: Keep che before the subordinate subject.
questions.speak: Penso che tu abbia ragione.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: I think it is true.
I doubt she will come.
I know it is true.

questions.explanation: Opinion and doubt invite a subjunctive; a factual claim with so che uses indicative.
questions.hint: Identify opinion, doubt or knowledge.
questions.speak: Penso che sia vero.

lessons.title: Wishes and reactions
lessons.outcome: I can express what I want or feel about another person’s action.
lessons.takeaway: Sono contento che and mi dispiace che express a reaction to another situation.

objectives.label: Wishes and reactions
objectives.explanation: When I want someone else to act, volere che takes a subjunctive clause. Sono contento che and mi dispiace che express a reaction to another situation.

teach.title: Different subjects
teach.body: When I want someone else to act, volere che takes a subjunctive clause.

examples.it: Voglio che tu venga con noi.
examples.en: I want you to come with us.

teach.title: Emotional response
teach.body: Sono contento che and mi dispiace che express a reaction to another situation.

examples.it: Sono contenta che tu stia meglio.
examples.en: I’m glad you are feeling better.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Voglio che voi ___ puntuali.
questions.translation: I want you all to be on time.
questions.explanation: Voglio che addresses a desired action by others, so use siate.
questions.hint: Use the voi present subjunctive of essere.
questions.speak: Voglio che voi siate puntuali.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Spero che Anna ___ presto.
questions.translation: I hope Anna gets well soon.
questions.explanation: Spero che introduces a wish about Anna; guarisca is subjunctive.
questions.hint: Use the present subjunctive of guarire.
questions.speak: Spero che Anna guarisca presto.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Mi dispiace che Marco non ___ venire.
questions.translation: I’m sorry Marco cannot come.
questions.explanation: Mi dispiace che expresses a reaction, so possa fits.
questions.hint: Use the present subjunctive of potere.
questions.speak: Mi dispiace che Marco non possa venire.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I am happy that you are here.
questions.answer: Sono felice che tu sia qui.
questions.explanation: The emotional reaction precedes che and sia.
questions.hint: Use the subjunctive of essere after the reaction.
questions.speak: Sono felice che tu sia qui.

lessons.title: It is important that
lessons.outcome: I can make an impersonal evaluation with che and a subjunctive.
lessons.takeaway: È importante partire presto needs no che clause if no separate subject is named.

objectives.label: It is important that
objectives.explanation: È importante che, è necessario che and è possibile che introduce a subjunctive clause. È importante partire presto needs no che clause if no separate subject is named.

teach.title: Evaluation plus clause
teach.body: È importante che, è necessario che and è possibile che introduce a subjunctive clause.

examples.it: È importante che tutti capiscano.
examples.en: It is important that everyone understands.

teach.title: Same subject often uses an infinitive
teach.body: È importante partire presto needs no che clause if no separate subject is named.

examples.it: È meglio partire adesso.
examples.en: It is better to leave now.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: È necessario che loro ___ subito.
questions.translation: It is necessary that they leave immediately.
questions.explanation: Partano is present subjunctive after è necessario che.
questions.hint: Use the loro present subjunctive after che.
questions.speak: È necessario che loro partano subito.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: È possibile che il treno ___ in ritardo.
questions.translation: It is possible that the train is late.
questions.explanation: Possibility is evaluated with a subjunctive clause.
questions.hint: Use the present subjunctive of essere.
questions.speak: È possibile che il treno sia in ritardo.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: È meglio ___ prima delle otto.
questions.translation: It is better to leave before eight.
questions.explanation: Without a separate subject, è meglio takes an infinitive.
questions.hint: Choose the infinitive after è meglio.
questions.speak: È meglio partire prima delle otto.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: It is important that you listen.
questions.explanation: È importante che requires the subjunctive ascolti.
questions.hint: Put the evaluation before che.
questions.speak: È importante che tu ascolti.

units.title: Say what depends on what
units.description: Distinguish likely conditions from imagined present situations.

lessons.title: If it happens
lessons.outcome: I can use se with an open, realistic condition.
lessons.takeaway: A future result may follow a present condition.

objectives.label: If it happens
objectives.explanation: For a possible situation, se normally takes indicative present or future, depending on time. A future result may follow a present condition.

teach.title: Real condition
teach.body: For a possible situation, se normally takes indicative present or future, depending on time.

examples.it: Se piove, restiamo a casa.
examples.en: If it rains, we stay home.

teach.title: Future in the result
teach.body: A future result may follow a present condition.

examples.it: Se finisci presto, ti chiamerò.
examples.en: If you finish early, I’ll call you.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se domani ___, prenderemo il treno.
questions.translation: If it rains tomorrow, we’ll take the train.
questions.explanation: An open future condition commonly uses present indicative after se.
questions.hint: Use present indicative for a realistic condition.
questions.speak: Se domani piove, prenderemo il treno.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Se hai tempo, ___ a cena con noi.
questions.translation: If you have time, come to dinner with us.
questions.explanation: An open condition can be followed by an invitation in the imperative.
questions.hint: Use the familiar imperative of venire.
questions.speak: Se hai tempo, vieni a cena con noi.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se non trovo le chiavi, ___ a casa.
questions.translation: If I do not find the keys, I will stay home.
questions.explanation: The realistic condition points to a future result.
questions.hint: Use future for the expected result.
questions.speak: Se non trovo le chiavi, resterò a casa.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: If you finish early, call me.
questions.explanation: Present indicative finisci expresses the realistic condition.
questions.hint: Put the se clause before the request.
questions.speak: Se finisci presto, chiamami.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: If it rains, I stay home.

pairs.left: Se piove domani, resterò a casa.
pairs.right: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home.
If it were raining, I would stay home.

questions.explanation: Real conditions use indicative; an imagined one uses imperfect subjunctive and conditional.
questions.hint: Use the verb forms and time marker.
questions.speak: Se piove, resto a casa.

lessons.title: If I had more time
lessons.outcome: I can imagine an unreal or unlikely present situation.
lessons.takeaway: The other clause takes present conditional. Do not put a conditional immediately after se in this standard pattern.

objectives.label: If I had more time
objectives.explanation: Use se plus imperfect subjunctive to present a contrary-to-fact or unlikely condition. The other clause takes present conditional. Do not put a conditional immediately after se in this standard pattern.

teach.title: Imagined condition
teach.body: Use se plus imperfect subjunctive to present a contrary-to-fact or unlikely condition.

examples.it: Se avessi più tempo, leggerei di più.
examples.en: If I had more time, I would read more.

teach.title: Imagined result
teach.body: The other clause takes present conditional. Do not put a conditional immediately after se in this standard pattern.

examples.it: Se fossi libero, verrei con voi.
examples.en: If I were free, I would come with you.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se ___ più soldi, comprerei una bici.
questions.translation: If I had more money, I would buy a bicycle.
questions.explanation: Avessi is imperfect subjunctive in the imagined condition.
questions.hint: Use imperfect subjunctive after se.
questions.speak: Se avessi più soldi, comprerei una bici.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Se abitassi vicino, ___ a piedi.
questions.translation: If I lived nearby, I would go on foot.
questions.explanation: Andrei is present conditional in the imagined result.
questions.hint: Use conditional of andare.
questions.speak: Se abitassi vicino, andrei a piedi.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Se tu ___ libero, usciremmo insieme.
questions.translation: If you were free, we would go out together.
questions.explanation: Fossi is the imperfect subjunctive required in the se clause.
questions.hint: Avoid the conditional directly after se.
questions.speak: Se tu fossi libero, usciremmo insieme.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: If I could, I would stay longer.
questions.explanation: Potessi states the imagined condition; resterei gives the result.
questions.hint: Use se plus subjunctive, then conditional.
questions.speak: Se potessi, resterei ancora.

units.title: Pass information on
units.description: Report statements and embedded questions without changing their meaning.

lessons.title: Say what someone said
lessons.outcome: I can report a statement with dire che and a clear point of view.
lessons.takeaway: When the reporting verb is present and the fact remains current, the subordinate often keeps its indicative tense.

objectives.label: Say what someone said
objectives.explanation: Dire che introduces the content of a statement. Adjust pronouns to the new speaker. When the reporting verb is present and the fact remains current, the subordinate often keeps its indicative tense.

teach.title: Statement into a clause
teach.body: Dire che introduces the content of a statement. Adjust pronouns to the new speaker.

examples.it: Marta dice: «Sono stanca». → Marta dice che è stanca.
examples.en: Marta says she is tired.

teach.title: Present reporting frame
teach.body: When the reporting verb is present and the fact remains current, the subordinate often keeps its indicative tense.

examples.it: Luca dice che arriva alle sei.
examples.en: Luca says that he is arriving at six.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Marta dice: «Ho fame». Marta dice che ___ fame.
questions.translation: Marta says, “I’m hungry.” Marta says that she is hungry.
questions.explanation: Marta becomes the subject in the reported clause, so use ha.
questions.hint: Shift first person to third person.
questions.speak: Marta dice: «Ho fame». Marta dice che ha fame.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Luca dice: «Parto domani». Luca dice che ___ domani.
questions.translation: Luca says, “I leave tomorrow.” Luca says that he leaves tomorrow.
questions.explanation: With present dice, the current plan can remain present; Luca takes third person.
questions.hint: Change parto to third person.
questions.speak: Luca dice: «Parto domani». Luca dice che parte domani.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Anna spiega: «Non conosco il quartiere». Anna spiega che non ___ il quartiere.
questions.translation: Anna explains that she does not know the neighborhood.
questions.explanation: The present report keeps the current fact; Anna requires conosce.
questions.hint: Use third-person present.
questions.speak: Anna spiega: «Non conosco il quartiere». Anna spiega che non conosce il quartiere.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: Marco says that he missed the train.
questions.answer: Marco dice che ha perso il treno.
questions.explanation: Che introduces the reported content after dice.
questions.hint: Place the reported clause after dice che.
questions.speak: Marco dice che ha perso il treno.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: Marta says she is tired.
Luca says he leaves tomorrow.

pairs.left: Anna spiega che non conosce la zona.
pairs.right: Anna explains she does not know the area.

questions.explanation: The content follows che, with person adjusted to the named speaker.
questions.hint: Check who is speaking in each sentence.
questions.speak: Marta dice che è stanca.

lessons.title: Ask what someone knows
lessons.outcome: I can embed a yes/no or wh-question after a reporting verb.
lessons.takeaway: Dove, quando and perché stay at the start of the embedded question; no question mark is needed in a statement.

objectives.label: Ask what someone knows
objectives.explanation: A direct yes/no question becomes a clause with se after chiedere or sapere. Dove, quando and perché stay at the start of the embedded question; no question mark is needed in a statement.

teach.title: Yes/no questions use se
teach.body: A direct yes/no question becomes a clause with se after chiedere or sapere.

examples.it: Mi chiede: «Parti?» → Mi chiede se parto.
examples.en: She asks me whether I am leaving.

teach.title: Keep the question word
teach.body: Dove, quando and perché stay at the start of the embedded question; no question mark is needed in a statement.

examples.it: Non so dove abita Paolo.
examples.en: I don’t know where Paolo lives.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Mi ha chiesto ___ avevo il biglietto.
questions.translation: She asked me whether I had the ticket.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is embedded with se.
questions.hint: Use the word for whether.
questions.speak: Mi ha chiesto se avevo il biglietto.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Sai ___ parte il treno? Alle sette.
questions.translation: Do you know when the train leaves? At seven.
questions.explanation: The answer gives a time, so the embedded question needs quando.
questions.hint: Ask for time.
questions.speak: Sai quando parte il treno? Alle sette.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Non ricordo ___ ho messo le chiavi.
questions.translation: I don’t remember where I put the keys.
questions.explanation: The missing information is a place, so use dove.
questions.hint: Ask for location.
questions.speak: Non ricordo dove ho messo le chiavi.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I do not know whether the shop is open.
questions.answer: Non so se il negozio è aperto.
questions.explanation: Se introduces an embedded yes/no question.
questions.hint: Place se after non so.
questions.speak: Non so se il negozio è aperto.

units.title: Keep the focus on the action
units.description: Use impersonal and passive forms when the actor is general or secondary.

lessons.title: People in general
lessons.outcome: I can express a general habit or rule with impersonal si.
lessons.takeaway: Si è plus a plural adjective for a generic group: quando si è stanchi.

objectives.label: People in general
objectives.explanation: Si plus a third-person verb can mean people in general or one. Si è plus a plural adjective for a generic group: quando si è stanchi.

teach.title: General subject
teach.body: Si plus a third-person verb can mean people in general or one.

examples.it: In Italia si cena spesso tardi.
examples.en: In Italy people often eat dinner late.

teach.title: With essere and adjectives
teach.body: Si è plus a plural adjective for a generic group: quando si è stanchi.

examples.it: Quando si è stanchi, si sbaglia più facilmente.
examples.en: When one is tired, one makes mistakes more easily.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: In biblioteca non ___ ad alta voce.
questions.translation: In the library people do not speak loudly.
questions.explanation: Impersonal si with parlare uses third-person singular here.
questions.hint: Use si before a singular verb.
questions.speak: In biblioteca non si parla ad alta voce.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: In questa città ___ bene.
questions.translation: People live well in this city.
questions.explanation: Si vive describes people in general.
questions.hint: Use si plus third-person singular of vivere.
questions.speak: In questa città si vive bene.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Quando ___ stanchi, è meglio riposare.
questions.translation: When people are tired, it is better to rest.
questions.explanation: Impersonal si with essere is si è; the adjective is plural.
questions.hint: Use si è before the plural adjective.
questions.speak: Quando si è stanchi, è meglio riposare.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: People eat well here.
questions.explanation: Si mangia makes a general statement without naming diners.
questions.hint: Put si before the verb.
questions.speak: Qui si mangia bene.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: People live well here.
People speak softly in the library.

pairs.left: Quando si è stanchi, si riposa.
pairs.right: When people are tired, they rest.

questions.explanation: Impersonal si makes a statement about people in general.
questions.hint: Each clause has no named actor.
questions.speak: Qui si vive bene.

lessons.title: What receives the action
lessons.outcome: I can make a present or completed passive statement.
lessons.takeaway: The actor can follow da, and the participle agrees with the new subject.

objectives.label: What receives the action
objectives.explanation: Passive essere plus past participle makes the object of an active verb the grammatical subject. The actor can follow da, and the participle agrees with the new subject.

teach.title: Focus on the affected thing
teach.body: Passive essere plus past participle makes the object of an active verb the grammatical subject.

examples.it: Il museo viene aperto alle nove.
examples.en: The museum is opened at nine.

teach.title: Agent with da
teach.body: The actor can follow da, and the participle agrees with the new subject.

examples.it: Le lettere sono state scritte da Anna.
examples.en: The letters were written by Anna.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: La porta ___ chiusa alle otto ogni sera.
questions.translation: The door is closed at eight every evening.
questions.explanation: Viene chiusa is a passive event with singular la porta.
questions.hint: Use singular passive auxiliary.
questions.speak: La porta viene chiusa alle otto ogni sera.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Le pizze ___ preparate ogni mattina.
questions.translation: The pizzas are prepared every morning.
questions.explanation: Le pizze is plural, so passive vengono agrees with it.
questions.hint: Use plural venire.
questions.speak: Le pizze vengono preparate ogni mattina.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Il ponte ___ costruito nel 1998.
questions.translation: The bridge was built in 1998.
questions.explanation: A completed passive event uses è stato plus the participle.
questions.hint: Match singular il ponte.
questions.speak: Il ponte è stato costruito nel 1998.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: The letter was signed by Maria.
questions.answer: La lettera è stata firmata da Maria.
questions.explanation: È stata firmata agrees with feminine singular lettera; da marks the agent.
questions.hint: Keep the participle feminine singular.
questions.speak: La lettera è stata firmata da Maria.

units.title: Link reasons and outcomes
units.description: Use clause links to explain purpose, results, contrast and event order.

lessons.title: Because or in order to
lessons.outcome: I can choose a reason or purpose clause according to meaning.
lessons.takeaway: Per plus infinitive expresses a purpose when the understood subject is the same.

objectives.label: Because or in order to
objectives.explanation: Perché plus an indicative fact can give the reason for an action. Per plus infinitive expresses a purpose when the understood subject is the same.

teach.title: Cause explains why
teach.body: Perché plus an indicative fact can give the reason for an action.

examples.it: Sono rimasto a casa perché pioveva.
examples.en: I stayed home because it was raining.

teach.title: Purpose gives the goal
teach.body: Per plus infinitive expresses a purpose when the understood subject is the same.

examples.it: Studio per superare l’esame.
examples.en: I study in order to pass the exam.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Ho acceso la luce ___ non vedevo bene.
questions.translation: I turned on the light because I could not see well.
questions.explanation: The poor visibility is the existing reason.
questions.hint: Choose the link meaning because.
questions.speak: Ho acceso la luce perché non vedevo bene.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Ho studiato tutta la sera ___ superare l’esame.
questions.translation: I studied all evening in order to pass the exam.
questions.explanation: Per plus infinitive expresses the goal of the same subject.
questions.hint: Use the preposition for purpose before an infinitive.
questions.speak: Ho studiato tutta la sera per superare l’esame.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Giulia non è uscita ___ aveva la febbre.
questions.translation: Giulia did not go out because she had a fever.
questions.explanation: The fever is the reason that already existed.
questions.hint: Use a reason clause with an indicative.
questions.speak: Giulia non è uscita perché aveva la febbre.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: I came in order to help you.
questions.explanation: Per aiutarti gives the purpose of coming.
questions.hint: Put per before the infinitive.
questions.speak: Sono venuta per aiutarti.

questions.prompt: Match each Italian expression with its meaning.
questions.translation: Choose the matching English meaning.

pairs.right: I stayed because it was raining.
I study in order to learn.
It rained, so we stayed.

questions.explanation: Perché gives cause, per plus infinitive purpose, and quindi result.
questions.hint: Identify reason, goal or consequence.
questions.speak: Sono rimasto perché pioveva.

lessons.title: Result and surprise
lessons.outcome: I can link a result or a fact that contrasts with expectation.
lessons.takeaway: Anche se introduces a real fact that did not stop the other event.

objectives.label: Result and surprise
objectives.explanation: A high degree may be followed by così...che to show what happened as a result. Anche se introduces a real fact that did not stop the other event.

teach.title: Result with così...che
teach.body: A high degree may be followed by così...che to show what happened as a result.

examples.it: Era così stanco che si è addormentato.
examples.en: He was so tired that he fell asleep.

teach.title: Concession with anche se
teach.body: Anche se introduces a real fact that did not stop the other event.

examples.it: Anche se piove, usciamo.
examples.en: Even though it is raining, we are going out.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Era ___ tardi che abbiamo preso un taxi.
questions.translation: It was so late that we took a taxi.
questions.explanation: Così...che marks degree followed by a result.
questions.hint: Choose the degree word before tardi.
questions.speak: Era così tardi che abbiamo preso un taxi.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: ___ era stanca, è venuta alla festa.
questions.translation: Even though she was tired, she came to the party.
questions.explanation: Anche se introduces a real obstacle that did not prevent coming.
questions.hint: Use the phrase meaning even though.
questions.speak: Anche se era stanca, è venuta alla festa.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: ___ non aveva fame, ha assaggiato la torta.
questions.translation: Although he was not hungry, he tasted the cake.
questions.explanation: The lack of hunger contrasts with tasting; anche se fits.
questions.hint: Choose a concession, not a cause.
questions.speak: Anche se non aveva fame, ha assaggiato la torta.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: It was raining, so we stayed home.
questions.answer: Pioveva, quindi siamo rimasti a casa.
questions.explanation: Quindi states the consequence of the rain.
questions.hint: Put the result after quindi.
questions.speak: Pioveva, quindi siamo rimasti a casa.

lessons.title: Before and after
lessons.outcome: I can sequence actions and choose infinitive or finite clauses.
lessons.takeaway: Use prima che plus subjunctive when the later event has its own subject. After a real completed event, dopo che commonly takes indicative.

objectives.label: Before and after
objectives.explanation: Use prima di plus infinitive when the same person does both actions. Use prima che plus subjunctive when the later event has its own subject. After a real completed event, dopo che commonly takes indicative.

teach.title: Same subject: prima di
teach.body: Use prima di plus infinitive when the same person does both actions.

examples.it: Prima di uscire, spengo le luci.
examples.en: Before going out, I switch off the lights.

teach.title: Different subjects: prima che
teach.body: Use prima che plus subjunctive when the later event has its own subject. After a real completed event, dopo che commonly takes indicative.

examples.it: Partiamo prima che arrivi Marco.
examples.en: We are leaving before Marco arrives.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Chiudi la finestra prima ___ uscire.
questions.translation: Close the window before going out.
questions.explanation: Same understood subject and infinitive require prima di.
questions.hint: Use prima di before an infinitive.
questions.speak: Chiudi la finestra prima di uscire.

questions.prompt: Type the missing Italian words.
questions.context: Andiamo via prima che il negozio ___.
questions.translation: Let us leave before the shop closes.
questions.explanation: Prima che introduces a separate subject and takes a subjunctive.
questions.hint: Use present subjunctive of chiudere.
questions.speak: Andiamo via prima che il negozio chiuda.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that completes the sentence.
questions.context: Dopo che ___ finito il lavoro, siamo usciti.
questions.translation: After we finished the work, we went out.
questions.explanation: A real completed event after dopo che takes indicative passato prossimo here.
questions.hint: Use a factual completed past.
questions.speak: Dopo che abbiamo finito il lavoro, siamo usciti.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this idea.
questions.translation: After eating, we went out.
questions.explanation: Dopo aver mangiato shows an earlier action by the same subject.
questions.hint: Put the completed infinitive clause first.
questions.speak: Dopo aver mangiato, siamo usciti.
